newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends down on forecasts for rain.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends down on forecasts for rain.

text.p: Forecasts for rain in France, an outlook for cool and damp weather in the U.S. Great Plains and skepticism about a report Tuesday that up to 290 million bushels of wheat were lost because of a recent freeze in the U.S. Great Plains, pressured KCBT hard red winter wheat futures to sharply lower closes, traders said.
"It's a weather market. That (French rain forecast) started the bears today and also the forecast for cool, damp weather in the Plains," a trader said.
Light rains are expected in western France by Friday and more substantial rain may be in store for the weekend.
But some say the rain may be too little too late.

Persistent cold, dry weather has already done some serious damage in France and experts now predict possible yield losses of 10 to 20 percent for winter grains, a crop expert for the French ACPA farm lobby told Reuters.
But the outlook for rain in the U.S. Plains was good news for wheat farmers there.
"They're saying the cooler and wetter weather will help the crop come back from the freeze," a trader said.
KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed 7-1/2 to 17-1/2 cents a bushel lower, with May down 13-1/2 at $4.83-1/2. July closed down 17-1/2 at $4.61-1/2.
Sell stops were hit in late trading when the July broke below support at the $4.65 a bushel level. "It was look out below when the sell stops were hit," the trader said.
Late selling was broad based and included commercial selling, the traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 36.92 million bushels, below the 50.065 million traded Tuesday.
